abstract: Hu, Wu, Li and Wang (COLT 2017) recorded an unresolved gap for the largest recursive teaching dimension (RTD) of finite (3,6) concept classes: binary classes on an arbitrary finite domain whose restriction to any three coordinates shows at most six patterns. The known bounds were 2 and 3; the upper bound comes from the minimum shattered-cell argument of Moran, Shpilka, Wigderson and Yehudayoff. We prove that every nonempty finite (3,6) class has a concept with a teaching set of size at most two. Since the property is inherited by subclasses, every such class has RTD at most 2, and f(3,6) = 2. The proof extends the minimum-cell argument with a short descent on one coordinate triple that turns three labels into two. The bound is attained by the six rows of {0,1}^3 other than 000 and 111. Warmuth's VC-2 class, with RTD 3, shows seven patterns on a triple, so the argument cannot extend to all VC-2 classes. Exhaustive local checks support every case of the proof. Bounded exclusion provides further checks: a SAT encoding excludes obstructions on up to 8 coordinates, while a separate encoding and a small-class reduction exclude up to 13 concepts on arbitrary finite domains; the retained UNSAT proofs were checked by a separate RUP checker. An independent audit with separately written code confirmed the proof and enumerated every class on at most five coordinates. We also note that an eight-concept example reported with RTD 4 in a university survey has RTD 2. A standard-library supplement reruns the local checks and the exact RTD computations. The search, proof and checks were produced by AI research agents with the author of record.
